answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to make identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify. Require every agent to stake a small deposit and build a reputation kernel: a verifiable history of completed work, peer attestations, and consistent behavior over time. Like light through a prism, a fake identity splits into inconsistent signals — mismatched logs, no trusted endorsements, erratic timing — while a real agent shows one coherent beam. Reputation should decay with inactivity, so an attacker cannot stockpile idle accounts on a terrace and activate them all at once.
